questions.text: You stumble on proof that a local boss is skimming money from the people under them. What do you do?

options.text: Stay quiet, build an airtight case, and bring them down when it hurts most.
Let them know you know — and name your price for silence.
Leak it anonymously and watch the fallout from a safe distance.
Find where the money goes and quietly redirect it to yourself.
Break in at night and take the ledger, and anything else worth taking.

questions.text: A rival makes a big mistake and leaves themselves exposed. Your move?

options.text: Don't rush. Set a trap that turns their mistake into total defeat.
Hit them now, hard, before they can recover.
Cut them off — no supplies, no backup, no way out.
Feed them bad information so they dig themselves in deeper.
Watch them for a while. Learn their habits, then strike where it hurts.

questions.text: The crew has one night to prepare for a job. How do you spend it?

options.text: Studying maps, schedules and guard rotations until the plan is airtight.
Cleaning, checking and tuning your weapons and gear.
Calling in favours: someone on the inside, a driver, a fence.
Working out how to blind the cameras and sensors before you go in.
Scouting the site from a rooftop until you know every blind spot.

questions.text: You're locked in a room and an alarm is counting down. How do you get out?

options.text: Smash through the door — or the wall.
Hack the door panel.
Talk the guard outside into opening it, or scare them into it.
Build something out of whatever is lying around.
Pick the lock with whatever you have in your pockets.

questions.text: How do you feel about rules?

options.text: Rules are full of gaps, and I know how to slip through them.
Rules get broken when they get in my way.
I don't care about rules, only about getting the job done.
Every system has patterns. Learn them and you can bend them.
Rules are for people with something to lose.

questions.text: The job is done, but it went badly and you barely made it out. What do you do first?

options.text: Go over every step to understand what went wrong.
Sell what you grabbed, fast, before anyone comes looking.
Fix the team's gear so it's ready for next time.
Erase every digital trace you left behind.
Disappear for a few days, then go back for what you left behind.

soldier.description: Built for frontline resilience, heavy physical capability, and tactical focus.

hacker.description: Cerebral specialist prioritizing digital mastery, social leverage, and mental fortitude.

techwiz.description: Pragmatic technician with deep environmental insight and technical resilience.

smuggler.description: Agile operator relying on quick reflexes, sharp social leverage, and street smarts.

scavenger.description: Hard to kill and hard to read: quick hands, patience and a mind for patterns.
